indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for pain is wrapped round the word for dope

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
pot is slang for cannabis, which is also called dope

explanation.surface: Someone observes a pain that came on without any drugs being taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: STING goes round POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting something is catching sight of it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Flatter a good man with real potential

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's good man

indicators.note: potential suggests what the letters could become, so the word real is rearranged

explanation.surface: A saintly man with real promise is offered flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges REAL to ALER, which follows ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatter here is the comparative of flat, as beer goes flat: more stale.

parts.note: nothing at all is zero, written as the letter O
to pine is to waste away or decline in health

explanation.surface: Nobody turned the offer down, so the conclusion is that it was believed.
explanation.definitionFit: Opined means gave an opinion, so it is a past-tense synonym of thought as in believed.

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering about, so the word Restrain is jumbled

explanation.surface: A call to hold back coaches who have been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are coaches who teach skills, so they are instructors.

clue.text: Time for reflection just the same

indicators.note: a word that reflects into the same word reads identically backwards, so the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A moment to stop and think, all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a time of day.

clue.text: Joining a party extremist much admired

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a red is a revolutionary, a political extremist

explanation.surface: A radical signing up to a political party wins great admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adored is to be loved and worshipped, deeply admired.

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale
earth is another word for soil

explanation.surface: A gardener records that the soil lacks something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, so it means deficiency.

parts.note: reads as a musical instrument needing its own score, but also hints at a person who keeps a tally or record

explanation.surface: A music teacher notes that a certain instrument needs its own part written.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind instrument played by schoolchildren, and also a person who writes down scores or minutes.

parts.note: assuming one's clothes is putting them on; personal cover could also be a bandage on a wound

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a suitable disguise or alias.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on clothes is the act of getting clothed, and a bandage on a wound has the same name.

clue.text: The cartoonist is a Roman, it turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests letters turned about into a new order, so a Roman and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's cartoonist is revealed to be an ancient Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who draws the frames of animated cartoons is a cartoonist.

explanation.surface: A comment on the French departing in an embarrassing way.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word for left is this one, and in English it has come to mean socially clumsy.

clue.text: The down-to earth approach is dividing the country

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the other word open, so is goes inside the word for country

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom or country

explanation.surface: A practical political policy is splitting the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being practical and facing facts as they are is a pragmatic outlook, a down-to-earth approach.

clue.text: Ordering off more than one player

definitions.text: Ordering off more than one player

parts.words: Ordering off more than one player
parts.note: sounds like a referee sending off players, but is a stage direction telling several actors to leave

explanation.surface: A referee sends off several footballers at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for they go out, the stage direction telling several actors to leave.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
stores are shops

explanation.surface: An item about shops dealing with goods brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something back is to return it, a verb sense shared by both words.

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
posed means sat still for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: An artist's model, faced with a job, kept perfectly still.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed is to face an opponent, so faced as in confronted.

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for Greek
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Argue that the Greek fancies some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with something is to struggle against it, to contend.

explanation.surface: Someone keen to take on the role of mourner at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means enthusiastic; as a noun or verb it is also an Irish wailing lament for the dead, so one who keens mourns.

clue.text: The sad outcome of rent reduction

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
a drop is a fall or reduction

explanation.surface: A landlord cuts the rent with sorry results.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed in sorrow, a falling drop of crying is the sad outcome.

parts.note: in the main seems to mean mostly, but the main is the sea, where this creature clings to hulls

explanation.surface: Mostly, a sycophant follows someone about.
explanation.definitionFit: A crustacean that fixes itself to ships and rocks at sea, and a word for a persistent hanger-on.

indicators.note: brewed suggests ingredients mixed together, so Pure ales is rearranged

explanation.surface: Unadulterated beer made for the drinker's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight and satisfaction are what is meant by both words.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the phrase the vanguard

explanation.surface: A man from Wales leads the advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Welsh form of the name John, so a typical Welsh name.

clue.text: To read alone can bring solace

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: Reading by oneself can be a comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone in grief is to offer them solace.

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to the firm as it now stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together, to stick.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of Artist are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter becomes upset and hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Strait as an adjective means narrow or hard, as in straitened circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning narrow or tight, hence hard, as in dire straits and straitened times.

clue.text: Agent holding back fish that's not active

indicators.note: holding means the agent word contains the other piece

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: back means the fish word is read in reverse

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A secret agent holds back a fish that has gone limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EEL into LEE, and 'holding' puts it inside SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy and sluggish, ready for bed, so not active.

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a number of hundreds

explanation.surface: A kidnap victim's family managed to raise hundreds to secure release.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, read here as 'hundreds'.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive is ransomed when money is handed over to free them.

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: off means wrong or spoiled, so the letters of steal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tints a painting and then sneaks away silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges STEAL to ASTEL, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft pale shade, such as baby blue, is a colour.

clue.text: Treachery must involve hurt for someone

indicators.note: involve means contain, so the letters sit inside the word Treachery

explanation.surface: Betrayal is bound to cause somebody pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull pain is a hurt, and to feel it is to hurt.

explanation.surface: Loud publicity stirred up by a gangland operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or loud fuss, and also a dishonest money-making scheme run by crooks.

clue.text: Account the cleric will find correct

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest, a cleric

explanation.surface: A church official audits the books and finds them in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and free from error means right, so correct.

clue.text: Scraps for birds left outside the church

indicators.note: left outside means placed round the outside, so the bird word goes round the church

parts.note: pies are magpies, a crossword staple for birds
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Bread scraps for birds are put out beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE is an old word for magpie.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments or bits of something are scraps.

clue.text: Bank having taken in little cash of late

indicators.note: taken in means containing, so the bank word goes round the cash word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin, a little cash

explanation.surface: A bank has lately been holding only a small amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in the period not long ago, lately.
